title: The One Rule of Web Accessibility

scenes.say: What is the single most important rule for building accessible web apps? Let’s break it down.

scenes.label: POUR
scenes.say: Start with the basics: WCAG is built on four principles. Perceivable, operable, understandable, and robust. Think of them as your accessibility checklist.
Use semantic HTML first, like nav or button. Only reach for ARIA when native elements can’t do the job. ARIA is powerful, but it’s a backup, not a replacement.
Next, test everything with just your keyboard. Tab moves you forward, shift tab goes back, and enter or space activates buttons. If you can’t use it without a mouse, it’s not accessible.

scenes.title: Test with NVDA
scenes.say: Finally, try a screen reader. Fire up NVDA or VoiceOver and listen. Does the order make sense? Are labels clear? That’s the real test.

scenes.question: Should you use ARIA for all UI elements?
scenes.right: No, use native HTML first. ARIA only fills gaps.
scenes.say: Here’s a common trap: should you use ARIA everywhere? No. Native HTML is best. Only use ARIA when you have no other option.
